case.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
case.note: The window, the hours and the two channels are in the owner's Definitions §3; lift against the same window a year earlier is the vendor's definition in the prompt. The month before gives $4,442 instead of $5,272.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-01: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?

WITH lunch AS (
  SELECT gross_sales_cents, created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago' AS local_time
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND channel IN ('in_store', 'square_online')
)
SELECT sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2026-08-03' AND '2026-08-30')
     - sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2025-08-03' AND '2025-08-30')
FROM lunch
WHERE extract(hour FROM local_time) BETWEEN 11 AND 13

trace.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
trace.answer:
Lunch brought in about $1,395.64 more during Lunch 20 than in the same four weeks last year. That is net sales of $34,888.20 versus $33,492.56, an increase of about 4.2%.

- **Period and filters:** I compared August 3–30, 2026 with August 3–30, 2025. Both cover lunch (11:00–13:59 Chicago time) on in-store and Square Online orders only, completed orders only. That is the promotion's window as your policy defines it [Definitions §3, The Lunch 20 Promotion] [Definitions §2, Lunch].
- **Net sales:** I counted net sales as gross sales minus discounts. I did not subtract refunds, because the refund query timed out.
- **Gross sales:** Gross sales rose from $34,989.77 to $40,261.46, which is $5,271.69 more.
- **Orders:** Orders rose from 1,194 to 1,414.
- **Discounts:** Discounts grew from $1,497.21 to $5,373.26. That is why the net gain is much smaller than the gross gain.

case.question: How many new customers did Lunch 20 bring in?
case.note: A promo order carries the Lunch 20 discount (Definitions §3), so first-timers whose first order was merely at lunch in August do not count: that reading gives 451, not 262. 331 of the 811 promo orders were unidentified and cannot be classified.

-- sql-02: How many new customers did Lunch 20 bring in?

SELECT count(*)
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (customer_id) discount_name
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY customer_id, created_at
) first_order
WHERE discount_name = 'Lunch 20'

case.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
case.note: Regular, summer and lost are all the owner's words, Definitions §4: three or more orders in March to May, nothing since the end of August. 177 of 599.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-03: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?

WITH visits AS (
  SELECT customer_id, (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago')::date AS local_day
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT count(*)
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM visits
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-05-31') >= 3
     AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day > '2026-08-31') = 0

case.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
case.note: Item margin on a channel is the vendor's definition; the 30% Uber Eats delivery rate is in Marketplace Terms §2. Pickled Vegetables at $1.55 a unit, Fried Egg next at $1.61.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-04: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?

SELECT i.name
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND o.channel = 'uber_eats'
  AND o.fulfillment_type = 'delivery'
  AND c.name = 'Sides'
GROUP BY i.name, i.cost_cents
ORDER BY avg(oi.unit_price_cents) * 0.70 - i.cost_cents
LIMIT 1

case.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
case.note: Net payout, the vendor's definition: card fees off in-store orders, 25% commission off DoorDash delivery. $30.11 against $27.47 an order, so $2.64 more in store despite the 25% marketplace markup.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-05: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?

WITH september AS (
  SELECT o.channel, o.fulfillment_type, o.gross_sales_cents,
         o.gross_sales_cents - o.discount_cents AS after_discount,
         coalesce(p.processing_fee_cents, 0) AS fee
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id AND p.status = 'completed'
  WHERE o.state = 'completed'
    AND date_trunc('month', o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') = '2026-09-01'
)
SELECT round(
    avg(after_discount - fee) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'in_store')
  - avg(after_discount - gross_sales_cents * 0.25) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'doordash' AND fulfillment_type = 'delivery')
)
FROM september

In September 2026, we kept about $2.64 more per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order. That covers completed orders only.

DoorDash menu prices already include the markup of up to 25% over in-store prices [Definitions §5, Marketplaces]. That is why the gap is smaller than the commission alone would suggest.

trace.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
trace.answer:
No. A promotional text can't go out at 10pm. The policy bars any text between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. If we don't know a customer's local time, we use Central time [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours]. A 10pm send would fall inside those hours. Schedule it between 9am and 8pm in the customer's local time instead.

Two other rules apply to any promotional text:
- It can only go to customers with verified SMS consent. Implied consent isn't enough, and anyone who has unsubscribed can't be texted [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].
- It must name the restaurant and end with "Reply STOP to opt out" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

- **Order not identified:** The orders data has no table number, so I couldn't find table 12's ticket. A search of in-store orders between $50 and $75 returned many that include pho, and nothing marked one as table 12's. The proposal therefore has no order attached.
- **What I need from you:** Send me the order ID, or the time the ticket was rung in. I can then match it and attach it to the comp request.
- **Weekly cap:** Total comps in a week should stay under 1% of that week's gross sales. If a week goes over, the owner reviews every comp from it [House Policy §2, Comps].
